events.name: Rise of Sumerian city-states
events.description: Growth of urban centers, writing and organized institutions in southern Mesopotamia.

events.name: Akkadian imperial expansion
events.description: Sargon of Akkad built an early territorial empire across Mesopotamia.

events.name: Third Dynasty of Ur established
events.description: Ur became the center of a highly administered Mesopotamian state.

events.name: Hammurabi consolidates Babylonia
events.description: Babylon expanded under Hammurabi and became a major Mesopotamian power.

events.name: Hittite sack of Babylon
events.description: A Hittite campaign ended the Old Babylonian dynasty.

events.name: Late Bronze Age disruptions
events.description: A period of warfare, migration and political disruption affected several eastern Mediterranean states.

events.name: Neo-Assyrian imperial expansion
events.description: Assyria developed a large militarized empire across the Near East.

events.name: Fall of Babylon to Cyrus
events.description: The Achaemenid conquest incorporated Babylon into the Persian Empire.

events.name: Battle of Marathon
events.description: Athenian forces defeated a Persian expeditionary force near Marathon.

events.name: Battle of Thermopylae
events.description: A Persian invasion force fought Greek defenders at Thermopylae.

events.name: Battle of Salamis
events.description: Greek naval forces defeated the Persian fleet near Salamis.

events.name: Alexanderian conquest of Persia
events.description: Macedonian armies conquered the Achaemenid Empire and reached deep into Asia.

events.name: Battle of Cannae
events.description: Hannibal won a major tactical victory over Rome during the Second Punic War.

events.name: Destruction of Carthage
events.description: Rome destroyed Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War.

events.name: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.description: Julius Caesar crossed into Italy with his army, beginning a civil war.

events.name: Battle of Actium
events.description: Octavian defeated the forces of Antony and Cleopatra in a decisive naval engagement.

events.name: Augustus becomes first Roman emperor
events.description: Octavian established the political order conventionally associated with the Roman Empire.

events.name: Vesuvius eruption and destruction of Pompeii
events.description: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and neighboring settlements.

events.name: Constantine wins at Milvian Bridge
events.description: Constantine defeated Maxentius and secured control of the western Roman Empire.

events.name: Edict of Milan
events.description: Imperial policy granted toleration to Christianity and other religions.

events.name: Roman Empire permanently divided
events.description: After Theodosius I, eastern and western imperial administrations developed separately.

events.name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.description: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire.

events.name: Justinianian reconquests
events.description: Eastern Roman armies reconquered parts of North Africa and Italy.

events.name: Hijra of Muhammad to Medina
events.description: Muhammad migrated from Mecca to Medina, an event central to the Islamic calendar.

events.name: Early Islamic conquests
events.description: Arab-Muslim armies rapidly expanded across the Middle East, North Africa and beyond.

events.name: Tang dynasty established
events.description: The Tang dynasty reunified much of China and oversaw a major period of expansion.

events.name: An Lushan Rebellion
events.description: A devastating rebellion severely weakened the Tang state.

events.name: Norman Conquest of England
events.description: William of Normandy defeated Harold II and established Norman rule in England.

events.name: First Crusade
events.description: Western European crusading armies campaigned in the eastern Mediterranean.

events.name: Magna Carta
events.description: English barons compelled King John to accept a charter limiting aspects of royal authority.

events.name: Mongol conquest begins in North China
events.description: Mongol forces expanded into the Jin and wider East Asian political system.

events.name: Mongol capture of Baghdad
events.description: Hülegü’s forces captured Baghdad, ending Abbasid political authority there.

events.name: Black Death reaches Europe
events.description: Plague spread through Europe and caused catastrophic mortality and social disruption.

events.name: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: Ottoman forces captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

events.name: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.description: Christopher Columbus reached Caribbean islands during a voyage sponsored by Castile.

events.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
events.description: Castile and Portugal agreed to a division of overseas spheres of expansion.

events.name: Lutheran Reformation begins
events.description: Martin Luther’s challenge to church practices helped initiate the Protestant Reformation.

events.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.description: Spanish and Indigenous allies defeated the Mexica state and captured its capital.

events.name: Magellan expedition begins
events.description: The expedition associated with Ferdinand Magellan began the first circumnavigation of Earth.

events.name: Battle of Lepanto
events.description: The Holy League defeated an Ottoman fleet in a major Mediterranean naval battle.

events.name: Defenestration of Prague
events.description: The Prague defenestration helped trigger the Bohemian Revolt and Thirty Years’ War.

events.name: Peace of Westphalia
events.description: Treaties ending major parts of the Thirty Years’ War reshaped European diplomacy.

events.name: Glorious Revolution
events.description: James II was displaced and William and Mary took the English throne.

events.name: American Declaration of Independence
events.description: Thirteen British colonies declared independence and formed a revolutionary state.

events.name: French Revolution begins
events.description: The French Revolution transformed the political and social order of France and Europe.

events.name: Storming of the Bastille
events.description: Revolutionaries seized the Bastille during the early French Revolution.

events.name: Haitian Revolution begins
events.description: Enslaved and free people launched a revolution that ultimately produced Haitian independence.

events.name: Napoleon’s coup of 18 Brumaire
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte helped overthrow the Directory and establish the Consulate.

events.name: Battle of Trafalgar
events.description: British naval forces defeated a combined French-Spanish fleet.

events.name: Battle of Waterloo
events.description: Coalition forces defeated Napoleon, ending his Hundred Days.

events.name: Congress of Vienna
events.description: European powers negotiated a post-Napoleonic settlement and balance of power.

events.name: Greek War of Independence begins
events.description: Greek revolutionaries began a successful struggle against Ottoman rule.

events.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
events.description: A major uprising challenged East India Company rule and led to direct British Crown administration.

events.name: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
events.description: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed during the process of Italian unification.

events.name: American Civil War begins
events.description: The United States entered a civil war following secession and conflict over the Union and slavery.

events.name: Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: The U.S. proclamation declared enslaved people in rebelling areas to be free as a wartime measure.

events.name: German Empire proclaimed
events.description: The German Empire was proclaimed after Prussian-led unification wars.

events.name: Berlin Conference
events.description: European powers negotiated rules for colonial claims in Africa.

events.name: Meiji Restoration
events.description: Political authority was reorganized around the emperor and Japan embarked on rapid institutional modernization.

events.name: Boxer Uprising
events.description: The anti-foreign and anti-Christian Boxer movement culminated in international military intervention.

events.name: Russian Revolution of 1905
events.description: Mass protest and political crisis forced concessions from the Russian imperial government.

events.name: First World War
events.description: A global war involving major alliances transformed borders, empires and societies.

events.name: February Revolution
events.description: Mass unrest and military breakdown led to the abdication of Nicholas II.

events.name: October Revolution
events.description: Bolshevik forces seized key government institutions in Petrograd.

events.name: Treaty of Versailles
events.description: The peace treaty imposed terms on Germany and helped establish the postwar settlement.

events.name: League of Nations established
events.description: The League of Nations began operating as an international organization after World War I.

events.name: Great Depression begins
events.description: A worldwide economic crisis produced severe unemployment, deflation and political disruption.

events.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
events.description: Japanese forces seized Manchuria and established Manchukuo.

events.name: Spanish Civil War begins
events.description: Military revolt developed into a major civil war involving foreign intervention.

events.name: Munich Agreement
events.description: Britain, France, Germany and Italy agreed to the transfer of the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia to Germany.

events.name: Second World War
events.description: A global war transformed political borders, economies and societies across multiple continents.

events.name: Operation Barbarossa
events.description: Germany launched its invasion of the Soviet Union.

events.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japanese forces attacked the U.S. Pacific Fleet base, bringing the United States into the Pacific War.

events.name: Battle of Stalingrad
events.description: The prolonged battle ended with the surrender of the German Sixth Army and became a major turning point on the Eastern Front.

events.name: Normandy landings
events.description: Allied forces established a major western European beachhead in Normandy.

events.name: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
events.description: The United States used an atomic bomb against Hiroshima during the final phase of the Pacific War.

events.name: United Nations founded
events.description: The United Nations was established as a new international organization after World War II.

events.name: Indian independence
events.description: British rule in India ended and the subcontinent was partitioned into new states.

events.name: NATO established
events.description: Twelve states signed the North Atlantic Treaty establishing a collective-defense organization.

events.name: People’s Republic of China proclaimed
events.description: The Chinese Communist Party established the People’s Republic of China after the civil war.

events.name: Korean War begins
events.description: War broke out on the Korean Peninsula and became an internationalized Cold War conflict.

events.name: Suez Crisis
events.description: The nationalization of the Suez Canal was followed by an Anglo-French-Israeli military intervention and international pressure for withdrawal.

events.name: Cuban Revolution triumph
events.description: Revolutionary forces overthrew the Batista government.

events.name: Berlin Wall constructed
events.description: East German authorities began constructing the Berlin Wall around West Berlin.

events.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.description: The United States and Soviet Union confronted each other over Soviet missiles in Cuba.

events.name: Apollo 11 Moon landing
events.description: Humans landed on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission.

events.name: Bangladesh independence war
events.description: Conflict in East Pakistan culminated in the creation of Bangladesh.

events.name: 1973 oil crisis
events.description: Oil supply restrictions and price increases produced a major global economic shock.

events.name: Fall of Saigon
events.description: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, ending the Vietnam War.

events.name: Iranian Revolution
events.description: A revolutionary movement overthrew the Pahlavi monarchy and established a new political order.

events.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: East German border restrictions collapsed and the Berlin Wall ceased functioning as a closed border.

events.name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.description: The Soviet Union ceased to exist and fifteen independent republics emerged.

events.name: Breakup of Yugoslavia
events.description: The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia entered a prolonged period of dissolution and armed conflict.

events.name: Rwandan genocide
events.description: A genocide in Rwanda killed large numbers of Tutsi and moderate Hutu civilians.

events.name: Euro introduced as accounting currency
events.description: The euro became an accounting currency for participating states before notes and coins entered circulation in 2002.

events.name: September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks in the United States prompted major changes in international security and warfare.

events.name: Iraq War begins
events.description: A U.S.-led coalition invaded Iraq, overthrowing the Ba’athist government.

events.name: Arab Spring begins
events.description: Protests and uprisings spread across several Arab states and produced varied political outcomes.

events.name: Russian annexation of Crimea
events.description: Russia took control of Crimea after the 2014 political crisis in Ukraine; the annexation was not recognized by Ukraine and many states.

events.name: COVID-19 pandemic declared
events.description: A global infectious disease pandemic produced widespread mortality, public-health measures and economic disruption.

places.name: Ur
places.description: Major Sumerian urban center near the Euphrates and a center of early state formation.

places.name: Babylon
places.description: Ancient city on the Euphrates and capital of several Babylonian states.

places.name: Nineveh
places.description: Ancient Assyrian capital on the Tigris near modern Mosul.

places.name: Persepolis
places.description: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.

places.name: Athens
places.description: Greek polis and major center of political, military and cultural development.

places.name: Sparta
places.description: Peloponnesian polis noted for its militarized social organization.

places.name: Rome
places.description: Capital of the Roman state and a central Mediterranean political center.

places.name: Carthage
places.description: Phoenician-founded city that became the center of a major Mediterranean power.

places.name: Alexandria
places.description: Mediterranean port founded by Alexander and major Hellenistic intellectual center.

places.name: Constantinople
places.description: Imperial capital founded as New Rome and later capital of the Byzantine Empire and Ottoman Empire.

places.name: Baghdad
places.description: Abbasid capital and major intellectual, commercial and political center.

places.name: Cordoba
places.description: Major city of al-Andalus and capital of the Caliphate of Córdoba.

places.name: Timbuktu
places.description: Important trans-Saharan commercial and scholarly center.

places.name: Venice
places.description: Maritime republic and major Mediterranean commercial center.

places.name: Kyiv
places.description: Major East European center associated with Kyivan Rus and later states.

places.name: Kraków
places.description: Major Polish political and cultural center.

places.name: Prague
places.description: Bohemian and later Czech political center on the Vltava.

places.name: Walls of Constantinople
places.description: Fortification system central to the defense and eventual Ottoman conquest of the city.

places.name: Tenochtitlan
places.description: Mexica imperial capital built on islands in Lake Texcoco.

places.name: Cusco
places.description: Capital and ceremonial center of the Inca Empire.

places.name: Istanbul
places.description: Ottoman imperial capital following the conquest of Constantinople.

places.name: Paris
places.description: Major French political and cultural center.

places.name: London
places.description: Political and commercial center of England and later the United Kingdom.

places.name: Amsterdam
places.description: Major Dutch commercial and financial center during the Dutch Golden Age.

places.name: Vienna
places.description: Habsburg imperial capital and major Central European diplomatic center.

places.name: Berlin
places.description: Prussian capital and later German imperial capital.

places.name: Washington, D.C.
places.description: Capital of the United States and seat of its federal government.

places.name: New York
places.description: Major Atlantic port and commercial center of the United States.

places.name: São Paulo
places.description: Major industrial and commercial city in Brazil.

places.name: Tokyo
places.description: Japanese political center, first as Edo and later as Tokyo.

places.name: Delhi
places.description: Major South Asian imperial and political center.

places.name: Beijing
places.description: Chinese imperial capital under the Ming and Qing dynasties.

places.name: Moscow
places.description: Russian political center that became capital of the Russian state and later USSR.

places.name: Cairo
places.description: Major Nile city and political center of Egypt.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.description: Ancient and enduring religious and political center.

places.name: Mecca
places.description: Islamic holy city and birthplace of Muhammad.

places.name: Medina
places.description: City where Muhammad established the early Muslim community after the Hijra.

people.name: Sargon of Akkad
people.description: Founder of the Akkadian Empire and one of the earliest known imperial rulers.

people.name: Hammurabi
people.description: Babylonian king associated with imperial expansion and a famous law collection.

people.name: Cyrus the Great
people.description: Founder of the Achaemenid Empire and conqueror of Babylon.

people.name: Darius I
people.description: Achaemenid ruler who consolidated the empire and sponsored major administrative works.

people.name: Leonidas I
people.description: Spartan king who commanded Greek defenders at Thermopylae.

people.name: Alexander the Great
people.description: Macedonian king whose conquests created a vast Hellenistic realm.

people.name: Hannibal Barca
people.description: Carthaginian commander who invaded Italy during the Second Punic War.

people.name: Julius Caesar
people.description: Roman general and statesman whose civil war helped end the Roman Republic.

people.name: Augustus
people.description: First Roman emperor and architect of the early imperial settlement.

people.name: Constantine the Great
people.description: Roman emperor who reunited the empire and supported Christianity.

people.name: Justinian I
people.description: Eastern Roman emperor associated with legal codification and Mediterranean reconquests.

people.name: Muhammad
people.description: Founder of Islam and leader of the early Muslim community.

people.name: Charlemagne
people.description: Frankish ruler crowned emperor in 800 and presided over a large western European realm.

people.name: William the Conqueror
people.description: Norman duke who conquered England in 1066 and became its king.

people.name: Saladin
people.description: Sultan who united major Muslim territories and defeated Crusader forces at Hattin.

people.name: Genghis Khan
people.description: Founder of the Mongol Empire and organizer of a major Eurasian conquest state.

people.name: Kublai Khan
people.description: Mongol ruler who founded the Yuan dynasty in China.

people.name: Ibn Battuta
people.description: Moroccan traveler whose journeys provide important descriptions of fourteenth-century societies.

people.name: Timur
people.description: Central Asian conqueror who founded the Timurid dynasty.

people.name: Joan of Arc
people.description: French military and religious figure associated with the Lancastrian phase of the Hundred Years’ War.

people.name: Mehmed II
people.description: Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 1453.

people.name: Isabella I of Castile
people.description: Queen of Castile whose reign coincided with the completion of the Reconquista and Columbus voyage.

people.name: Christopher Columbus
people.description: Navigator whose 1492 voyage under Castilian sponsorship reached the Caribbean.

people.name: Leonardo da Vinci
people.description: Italian artist, engineer and polymath of the Renaissance.

people.name: Martin Luther
people.description: German theologian whose writings helped initiate the Protestant Reformation.

people.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
people.description: Ottoman sultan during a period of major imperial expansion and legal reform.

people.name: Galileo Galilei
people.description: Astronomer and physicist central to the Scientific Revolution.

people.name: William Shakespeare
people.description: English playwright and poet whose works became central to the English literary canon.

people.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
people.description: Japanese daimyo who established the Tokugawa shogunate.

people.name: Johannes Gutenberg
people.description: European printer traditionally associated with the spread of movable-type printing in Europe.

people.name: Peter the Great
people.description: Russian ruler who transformed institutions and expanded the Russian state.

people.name: Catherine the Great
people.description: Empress of Russia during territorial expansion and administrative reform.

people.name: George Washington
people.description: Military commander of the American Revolution and first U.S. president.

people.name: Thomas Jefferson
people.description: American statesman and principal drafter of the Declaration of Independence.

people.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
people.description: French military and political leader who became emperor and reshaped Europe through war and administration.

people.name: Simón Bolívar
people.description: Military and political leader associated with independence movements in northern South America.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.description: U.S. president during the Civil War who issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

people.name: Queen Victoria
people.description: British monarch whose reign coincided with industrialization and imperial expansion.

people.name: Otto von Bismarck
people.description: Prussian statesman who drove German unification and served as first imperial chancellor.

people.name: Florence Nightingale
people.description: Nursing reformer associated with changes in military and civilian medical care.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.description: Indian independence leader associated with mass nonviolent political action.

people.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
people.description: Founder of the Republic of Turkey and leader of major state reforms after the Ottoman collapse.

people.name: Woodrow Wilson
people.description: U.S. president during World War I and advocate of the League of Nations.

people.name: Vladimir Lenin
people.description: Bolshevik revolutionary and head of the Soviet government after 1917.

people.name: Joseph Stalin
people.description: Soviet leader during forced industrialization, collectivization and World War II.

people.name: Winston Churchill
people.description: British prime minister during much of World War II and a major wartime statesman.

people.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
people.description: U.S. president during the Great Depression and most of World War II.

people.name: Charles de Gaulle
people.description: French general and leader of Free France during World War II, later president of France.

people.name: Hideki Tojo
people.description: Japanese general and prime minister during much of the Pacific War.

people.name: Harry S. Truman
people.description: U.S. president at the end of World War II and during the early Cold War.

people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
people.description: First prime minister of independent India and a prominent non-aligned statesman.

people.name: Mao Zedong
people.description: Chinese Communist leader and founding leader of the People’s Republic of China.

people.name: Nelson Mandela
people.description: Anti-apartheid leader and first president of South Africa elected after the end of apartheid.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
people.description: Civil-rights leader associated with nonviolent activism in the United States.

people.name: John F. Kennedy
people.description: U.S. president during a major phase of the Cold War, including the Cuban Missile Crisis.

people.name: Nikita Khrushchev
people.description: Soviet leader during de-Stalinization and the Cuban Missile Crisis.

people.name: Ronald Reagan
people.description: U.S. president during the later Cold War.

people.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
people.description: Soviet leader associated with perestroika, glasnost and the final years of the USSR.

people.name: Deng Xiaoping
people.description: Chinese leader associated with economic reforms beginning in the late 1970s.
